subtopics.title: Bar Graphs and Histograms — Cousins, Not Twins

questions.question: In a bar graph the bars are drawn with gaps between them because:
options: the data are continuous and the intervals touch
the categories are separate labels, not neighbouring amounts on a number line
the bars would otherwise be too tall to fit

questions.question: Of the 300 learners surveyed, 135 travel by taxi. What percentage is that?
In the data-spend histogram (8, 15, 21, 10 and 6 learners), the modal class is:
How many of the 60 learners spend less than R100 on data per month?

subtopics.title: Pie Charts — Reading Shares, Not Amounts

questions.question: How many degrees represent 1 percent on a pie chart?
Food takes 30 percent of the household's income. What angle does its sector occupy?
A transport sector measures 54 degrees on a pie chart of a R12 000 income. How much is spent on transport?
Why can two pie charts not be compared slice for slice?
options: Because angles cannot be measured accurately
Because pie charts always exaggerate the largest sector
Because equal percentages of different totals represent different amounts of money
Because a pie chart may show only four sectors

subtopics.title: Line and Broken-Line Graphs — Change Over Time

questions.question: Monthly electricity units are 250, 240, 260, 310, 420 and 480 from January to June. Between which two months is the line steepest?
What is the total number of units bought over the six months?
At a tariff of R2,80 per unit, what did June's 480 units cost?
Why is a monthly meter reading shown as a broken-line graph rather than a solid continuous line?
options: Because the readings exist only at separate moments, so the joining lines show trend rather than real in-between values
Because broken lines are easier to draw
Because electricity use is categorical data
Because a solid line may only be used for temperature

subtopics.title: Choosing a Display — and Catching a Misleading One

questions.question: Which display best shows how one household's single monthly income is divided among its expenses?
Bars for 420 and 480 units are drawn on an axis starting at 400. What is the honest percentage increase?
Which of these is NOT one of the five things every honest display must carry?
options: The number of people who drew it

questions.question: What three moves make a full answer to a "criticise this graph" question?
options: Draw it again, colour it, label it
Identify the feature, explain the distortion, give the honest figure
State the mean, the median and the mode
Name the axis, the title and the source

subtopics.title: Bars With Gaps, Bars That Touch

questions.question: The Simplifier's one-second test for telling the two kinds of bars apart is:
options: look along the bottom axis: words mean gaps, numbers in order mean the bars touch

questions.question: Why is it acceptable to swap the walkers' bar and the bus riders' bar around?
options: Because the frequencies are close together
Because they are separate categories, so the order carries no meaning
Because bar graphs must be drawn from tallest to shortest

questions.question: Data spending is grouped into bands because:
options: rands run in a line, so R49 and R51 are neighbours rather than different categories
there were only 60 learners in the survey
money may never be shown on a graph

questions.question: In the plate-of-pap picture, what does the whole plate always represent?
options: The whole amount being divided — here R12 000, or 100 percent

questions.question: Housing takes 25 percent of R12 000. In rands and degrees, that slice is:
A neighbour's food slice is also 30 percent, but her income is R6 000. What does this show?
options: That her pie chart is drawn incorrectly
That equal-looking slices can buy very different amounts, so the total must be known
That her food costs the same, R3 600
That percentages cannot be used on pie charts

questions.question: Which check does the Simplifier insist on for every pie chart?
options: That the largest slice comes first
That there are no more than six slices
That the rand amounts total the income and the percentages total 100
That every slice is labelled in degrees

subtopics.title: The Winter Line, and the Graph That Lies

questions.question: Electricity use rises from 250 units in January to 480 in June. The Simplifier's practical advice to the household is:
options: stop buying prepaid electricity in winter
start setting money aside from about March, not June
use the mode instead of the mean

questions.question: Cutting the bottom off a vertical axis misleads because:
options: it removes the title of the graph
it makes a small difference between bars look enormous
it turns a bar graph into a histogram

questions.question: A picture drawn twice as tall AND twice as wide misleads because:
options: it looks four times as big, though it stands for only double
it can only be used for categorical data

questions.question: Which questions does the Simplifier tell you to run on any graph before trusting it?
options: Whether the mean equals the median
Where the scale starts, whether the gaps are even, whether the axes are labelled with units, and whether the total is given
